description:
Run a program of yours when something happens to you (a hook; only yours, your definition does not change). Changes work from the next event. The program is a tool folder or an executable; it gets the event as JSON on stdin (with "event", "hook", "stack" and the fields below). Events:
- before_queue: a message is about to enter your conversation (fields letter, content)
- after_queue: a message entered your conversation (letter, content)
- before_tool: one of your tools is about to run (name, id, arguments)
- after_tool: a tool finished, before you see its result (name, id, arguments, content, code, timed_out)
- brain_failed: your brain call failed (name = the error code, reason; error = the kernel's error object when there is one; on BrainFailed also retry (true = the same request is sent again after a wait, false = you stop), attempt (failures in a row), code and status (the kernel's code, the HTTP status) when the kernel gave them, and wait_s (seconds until the next try) when retry is true; on an eca with claude (CliFailed, ReplyMissing) also code, retry, attempt, dropped (letters dropped), wait_s when retrying, and status and cause (the CLI's own failure cause) when known; an eca with codex has only name and reason)
- tool_added: a tool name appeared in your tool box (name, path)
- before_compact: your conversation is about to be compacted (asked = the words after /compact, instructions = extra summary instructions you may change, restore = text you may give to add back after the summary; exit 10 blocks it); on agent-fsm also letters, mid_turn, foldable, clear (set false to keep old tool outputs) and summary (give one and the brain is not asked); on an eca with claude (Claude Code compacts) also trigger = manual or auto
- after_compact: the summary is ready (summary); on agent-fsm it is not in yet: also letters, by (brain or the hook that gave the summary), mid_turn, cleared and restore, and you may change summary and restore (restore = text added as one message right after the summary); on an eca with claude it only tells (trigger, summary)
- after_start: your loop started; after_stop: your loop is about to exit (the event has only event, hook and stack; the environment has AOS_LOOP_CODE, AOS_LOOP_SIGNAL and AOS_LOOP_CAUSE: stop|sleep|remove|shutdown|stuck|signal|max|body_exit|error, empty when not given; cause is a code to match, not the table's reason, which is a sentence for people; hitting a limit has no value of its own: look at limit_hit on the table; error is only a kind of stop, not an error code)
- before_run: before each run of your loop (each state of a state-machine agent, each turn of an eca), only when your definition's loop.json wires it (else you get a warning: it needs a recompile and a restart); exit 10 skips that run. The event has only event, hook and stack; the run number is in the environment (AOS_LOOP_RUNS), a state machine's state about to run in STACK/stage.txt
- after_run: after each run (wired the same way); environment AOS_LOOP_RUNS, AOS_LOOP_RUN_CODE, AOS_LOOP_RUN_SIGNAL, AOS_LOOP_RUN_MS
- on_clock: a clock moved on: give every_cycles or every_ms (counted in clock cycles); clock is optional (default: your daemon's clock); fields clock, cycle, interval_ms, first, last_cycle, missed, and config when the hook has one. It runs once right after you start or wake up, then every N. It shows you nothing; to hear about it, let the program send a letter to your queue (aos-post send STACK/queue).
One op per call:
- list: {"op": "ls"}  (add "long": true to also see hooks you turned off)
- show one: {"op": "get", "name": "guard"}
- add: {"op": "add", "event": "before_tool", "path": "hooks/guard", "condition": "agents_ctl"}  (relative paths start at your workspace; condition = only for this tool name or error code)
- on_clock with config: {"op": "add", "event": "on_clock", "every_ms": 5000, "name": "context_wrap", "path_json": {"$env": "AOS_HOME", "$path": "/lib/tools/agent/context_wrap"}, "config": {"percent": 50}, "timeout_ms": 20000, "replace": true}  (config = any JSON the program gets as the event field config)
- remove: {"op": "rm", "name": "guard"}
- back to your original hooks: {"op": "reset"}
What the program answers: exit 0 with empty stdout = no change; on before_queue, before_tool, after_tool, before_compact and after_compact a JSON object on stdout changes the event (content, arguments for before_tool, the keys named above for the compact events); exit 10 blocks before_queue, before_tool and before_compact (the message is dropped / the tool does not run / nothing is compacted) and skips a before_run run. Any other exit code (or too slow, or bad stdout) is a failure: on before_queue and before_tool you stop, on the other events it is only a warning, on after_start / after_stop / before_run / after_run your loop stops.
Errors: ArgumentsBad, OpUnknown, PathMissing, HookExists (add "replace": true to replace it), HookMissing, HooksMissing, HooksBad, NameBad, DaemonMissing, DaemonFailed, InstanceMissing.

op.description: ls = list, get = show one, add = add one, rm = remove one, reset = undo all your changes

name.description: get, rm: the hook name. add: the name to call it by (default: the folder or file name; needed with path_json)

event.description: add: the event that runs it

path.description: add: the tool folder or executable to run; relative paths start at your workspace

path_json.description: add, instead of path: a value kept as written, like {"$env": "AOS_HOME", "$path": "/lib/x"}

condition.description: add: run only for this tool name (before_tool, after_tool, tool_added) or error code (brain_failed), or an array of them

timeout_ms.description: add: give up waiting after this many ms (default 60000; 0 = no limit)

replace.description: add: true replaces a hook you already have with the same name

long.description: ls: true = one text line per hook with all its settings, including hooks you turned off (null)

every_cycles.description: add, on_clock only: run when the clock moved this many cycles since the last run

every_ms.description: add, on_clock only: the same in ms, counted in clock cycles (not the wall clock)

clock.description: add, on_clock only: a proc name on your daemon table whose stack has a clock file, or the path of a clock file or a folder with one (relative = from your stack); default your daemon's clock (AOS_CLOCK)

config.description: add, on_clock only: any JSON kept in the entry as config; the program gets it as the event's config field (e.g. context_wrap: {"percent": 50, "wrap": true})
